audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as Job's response to Bildad: impossibility of litigating with God, cosmic power, legal imagery, innocence under overwhelming force, and longing for a mediator/umpire.

verses.restored: Job answered and said:

familiar.text: Then Job answered and said,

verses.restored: Truly I know it is so; but how can a mortal be righteous with the Divine?

familiar.text: I know it is so of a truth: but how should man be just with God?

verses.restored: If one desired to contend with him, he could not answer him one time out of a thousand.

familiar.text: If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one of a thousand.

verses.restored: Wise in heart and strong in power, who has hardened himself against him and been whole?

familiar.text: He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who hath hardened himself against him, and hath prospered?

verses.restored: He removes mountains, and they do not know it, when he overturns them in his anger.

familiar.text: Which removeth the mountains, and they know not: which overturneth them in his anger.

verses.restored: He shakes the earth from its place, and its pillars tremble.

familiar.text: Which shaketh the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble.

verses.restored: He commands the sun, and it does not rise; he seals up the stars.

familiar.text: Which commandeth the sun, and it riseth not; and sealeth up the stars.

verses.restored: He alone stretches out the heavens and treads on the waves of the sea.

familiar.text: Which alone spreadeth out the heavens, and treadeth upon the waves of the sea.

verses.restored: He makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the chambers of the south.

familiar.text: Which maketh Arcturus, Orion, and Pleiades, and the chambers of the south.

verses.restored: He does great things beyond searching, and wonders without number.

familiar.text: Which doeth great things past finding out; yea, and wonders without number.

verses.restored: Look, he passes by me, and I do not see; he moves on, but I do not perceive him.

familiar.text: Lo, he goeth by me, and I see him not: he passeth on also, but I perceive him not.

verses.restored: Look, he snatches away; who can turn him back? Who can say to him, What are you doing?

familiar.text: Behold, he taketh away, who can hinder him? who will say unto him, What doest thou?

verses.restored: The Divine will not turn back his anger; beneath him bowed the helpers of Rahab.

familiar.text: If God will not withdraw his anger, the proud helpers do stoop under him.

verses.restored: How then can I answer him, choosing my words with him?

familiar.text: How much less shall I answer him, and choose out my words to reason with him?

verses.restored: Though I were righteous, I could not answer; I would plead for favor from my judge.

familiar.text: Whom, though I were righteous, yet would I not answer, but I would make supplication to my judge.

verses.restored: If I called and he answered me, I would not believe that he was listening to my voice.

familiar.text: If I had called, and he had answered me; yet would I not believe that he had hearkened unto my voice.

verses.restored: For he crushes me with a storm and multiplies my wounds for nothing.

familiar.text: For he breaketh me with a tempest, and multiplieth my wounds without cause.

verses.restored: He will not let me take my breath, but fills me with bitterness.

familiar.text: He will not suffer me to take my breath, but filleth me with bitterness.

verses.restored: If it is a matter of strength, look, he is mighty; if of justice, who will summon him?

familiar.text: If I speak of strength, lo, he is strong: and if of judgment, who shall set me a time to plead?

verses.restored: Though I were righteous, my own mouth would condemn me; though I were whole, it would declare me twisted.

familiar.text: If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me: if I say, I am perfect, it shall also prove me perverse.

verses.restored: I am whole; I do not know my soul. I reject my life.

familiar.text: Though I were perfect, yet would I not know my soul: I would despise my life.

verses.restored: It is all one; therefore I say, He brings the whole and the wicked to an end.

familiar.text: This is one thing, therefore I said it, He destroyeth the perfect and the wicked.

verses.restored: When a scourge kills suddenly, he laughs at the testing of the innocent.

familiar.text: If the scourge slay suddenly, he will laugh at the trial of the innocent.

verses.restored: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; he covers the faces of its judges. If not he, then who?

familiar.text: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, and who is he?

verses.restored: My days are swifter than a runner; they flee away; they see no good.

familiar.text: Now my days are swifter than a post: they flee away, they see no good.

verses.restored: They pass by like reed boats, like an eagle swooping on prey.

familiar.text: They are passed away as the swift ships: as the eagle that hasteth to the prey.

verses.restored: If I say, I will forget my complaint, leave my face, and brighten up,

familiar.text: If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will leave off my heaviness, and comfort myself:

verses.restored: I become afraid of all my pains; I know you will not hold me innocent.

familiar.text: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that thou wilt not hold me innocent.

verses.restored: I am declared wicked; why then do I labor in vain?

familiar.text: If I be wicked, why then labour I in vain?

verses.restored: If I wash myself with snow water and cleanse my hands with lye,

familiar.text: If I wash myself with snow water, and make my hands never so clean;

verses.restored: then you would plunge me into the pit, and my own garments would abhor me.

familiar.text: Yet shalt thou plunge me in the ditch, and mine own clothes shall abhor me.

verses.restored: For he is not a man like me, that I might answer him, that we might come together in judgment.

familiar.text: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, and we should come together in judgment.

verses.restored: There is no mediator between us, who might lay his hand on us both.

familiar.text: Neither is there any daysman betwixt us, that might lay his hand upon us both.

verses.restored: Let him remove his rod from me, and let his terror not frighten me.

familiar.text: Let him take his rod away from me, and let not his fear terrify me:

verses.restored: Then I would speak and not fear him, for I am not so within myself.

familiar.text: Then would I speak, and not fear him; but it is not so with me.
